body:
Found by the pre-release refuter loop gating v4.1.31, via a live A/B against the
pre-fix image. #947 itself is genuinely FIXED (76 EPERM -> 0, /login 000 -> 200,
all 9 s6 call sites converted, root path unregressed). These are the gaps that
remain inside "runs as non-root".

MEASUREMENT CAVEAT (important for any future verification of this area): the
"0 EPERM" figure was taken on Docker Desktop for macOS, where the /config bind
mount is fakeowner and does NOT enforce ownership. On a real kernel the ~10
`install -d -o abc -g abc` calls at root/etc/s6-overlay/s6-rc.d/cwa-init/run:
89-95,107-108,169 each still fail. Proved with a control on the container's own
filesystem, which bypasses fakeowner:

  docker exec --user 1000:1000 ... install -d -o abc -g abc /tmp/probe/x
  install: cannot change owner and permissions of '/tmp/probe/x': Operation not permitted
  rc=1;  drwx------ 2 1000 1000  /tmp/probe/x

Not fatal (dirs are still created, 0700 owned by the running uid is functionally
fine since everything runs as that uid), but the reporter @KucharczykL is on
podman, so "say it once instead of a screenful" is only partly met there. Do not
put a "0 EPERM" claim in user-facing notes.

Three residual non-root failures that are real -- they hit /etc and /app, so
fakeowner does not mask them:

1. cwa-init/run:32-33 -- rm: cannot remove '/etc/ImageMagick-6/policy.xml':
   Permission denied, then ln: File exists. The non-root container falls back to
   Ubuntu's stock ImageMagick policy instead of /defaults/policy.xml.
2. cwa-init/run:46 -- mkdir: cannot create '/app/calibre-web-automated/cps/cache':
   Permission denied. The dir does not exist in the image; it is created at
   runtime as root. Harmless as the code stands, because every fs.FileSystem()
   caller (cps/helper.py:1423,1560,1619, cps/kobo.py:1817) passes
   CACHE_TYPE_THUMBNAILS, which routes to CONFIG_DIR/thumbnails (cps/fs.py:27-28),
   and the CACHE_DIR branch has no callers. It becomes a live bug the moment a
   non-thumbnail cache type is added, because get_cache_dir re-raises on OSError
   (cps/fs.py:36). Note scripts/set_ownership.sh:33-35 asserts "cps/cache is
   created and chowned earlier in the cwa-init unit" -- untrue on this path.
3. [cwa-auto-library]: ERROR: Could not update dirs.json ... Permission denied.
   Changing the library location is unavailable when running non-root, because
   dirs.json lives in the abc-owned app tree.

Two smaller ones from the same pass:

4. scripts/set_ownership.sh:53 CWA_UID="${CWA_UID:-$(id -u)}" is env-overridable,
   and cwa-init/run:274 invokes it under with-contenv, so
   `docker run -e CWA_UID=1000` on a ROOTFUL container silently skips the entire
   ownership pass. CWA_UID appears nowhere user-facing (docs/, README.md,
   wiki-src/, local-dev/ all clean) and exists as the test seam
   (test_947_non_root_container_starts.py:169), so exposure is low -- but a
   distinctly-named override would be tighter.
5. The discriminator is `id -u = 0`, not "can I setgroups". A rootful container
   run with --cap-drop=SETGID still takes the drop branch and still crash-loops.
   Nobody has reported it.

Coverage gap: tests/unit/test_995_metadata_dirs_under_config.py:192 skips on
macOS ("cover_enforcer.py --help exited 2 in this environment"). That is the test
guarding the ModuleNotFoundError class the #995 note calls the expensive silent
failure, so it is not exercised on a developer host.
title: Non-root container start leaves three real residual failures (ImageMagick policy, cps/cache, dirs.json) and the 0-EPERM claim is a Docker Desktop fakeowner artifact
